days.title: Classic Ascent from the North
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Macgillycuddy’s Reeks
stops.detail: It is located in the southwest of the island in County Kerry and belongs to the Macgillycuddy's Reeks.

stops.name: Cronins Yard
stops.detail: The mountain is usually climbed from the north from the Cronins Yard hiking car park along Hag's Glen and via the steep, water-bearing Devil's Ladder and then over the southeast ridge.

stops.name: Devil’s Ladder
stops.detail: Sure-footedness and good mountain boots are, however, appropriate in the Devil's Ladder.

days.title: Rugged Ridges and Gully Routes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Brother O’Shea’s Gully
stops.detail: A difficult ascent "Brother O’Shea's Gully" leads via the northwest ridge, where two easy climbing sections of grade I must be overcome to reach the summit.

stops.name: Collins’ Gully
stops.detail: To the left of it, separated by Collins' Gully, lies Pipets Ridge and to the right of it Primroses Ridge.

days.title: Spectacular High Altitude Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Howling Ridge
stops.detail: Howling Ridge is considered one of the most spectacular and popular climbing routes in the country.

stops.name: Heavenly Gates
stops.detail: The Howling Ridge route begins at a high-elevation viewpoint referred to as the "Heavenly Gates".
